questions.question: What is the primary architectural advantage of React Server Components (RSC) in full-stack frameworks like Next.js?
options: They execute code only on the server, eliminating zero client bundle size for imported dependencies and allowing direct DB/filesystem access
They replace SQL databases with client localStorage
They require all components to be class-based
They automatically deploy websites to mobile app stores
questions.answer: They execute code only on the server, eliminating zero client bundle size for imported dependencies and allowing direct DB/filesystem access
questions.explanation: Server Components render exclusively on the server, streaming HTML and serialized flight payloads to the client without sending their package dependencies.

questions.question: Why should sensitive session authentication tokens be stored in 'httpOnly' cookies rather than browser 'localStorage'?
options: httpOnly cookies are automatically encrypted by the browser
httpOnly cookies are inaccessible to client-side JavaScript, mitigating session theft via Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
localStorage cannot store more than 10 bytes
httpOnly cookies cannot expire
questions.answer: httpOnly cookies are inaccessible to client-side JavaScript, mitigating session theft via Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
questions.explanation: If an attacker executes malicious JavaScript via an XSS vulnerability, httpOnly prevents script access to document.cookie.

questions.question: What header is required on Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) preflight requests for complex HTTP calls?
options: OPTIONS
TRACE
CONNECT
PATCH
questions.explanation: Browsers automatically send an HTTP OPTIONS preflight request before executing complex cross-origin requests to check allowed methods and headers.

questions.question: In GraphQL, what is the 'N+1 Problem' during relationship resolution?
options: A syntax error when querying more than N fields
An antipattern where fetching a list of N parent items causes the server to execute N additional independent database queries for related child data
Having N+1 servers in a cluster
A schema type recursion overflow
questions.answer: An antipattern where fetching a list of N parent items causes the server to execute N additional independent database queries for related child data
questions.explanation: Without batching mechanisms like DataLoader, naive nested field resolvers execute an individual query for every item in a collection.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Database Connection Pooling in serverless compute environments?
options: To merge all SQL queries into a single string
To reuse an active pool of database connections across ephemeral serverless invocations and prevent exhausting database connection limits
To backup database tables to CSV
To bypass database authentication
questions.answer: To reuse an active pool of database connections across ephemeral serverless invocations and prevent exhausting database connection limits
questions.explanation: Serverless functions scale rapidly by spawning hundreds of independent instances. Without proxy poolers (PgBouncer/Supabase Pooler), maximum connection limits are rapidly exhausted.

questions.question: In WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events (SSE), when is SSE technically preferable?
options: When real-time low-latency audio streaming in both directions is required
When the application only requires unidirectional server-to-client updates (e.g., AI streaming text, stock tickers) over standard HTTP/2 with built-in auto-reconnection
When WebSocket ports are wide open
When client browsers do not support JavaScript
questions.answer: When the application only requires unidirectional server-to-client updates (e.g., AI streaming text, stock tickers) over standard HTTP/2 with built-in auto-reconnection
questions.explanation: SSE runs over standard HTTP, multiplexes over HTTP/2, includes native browser reconnection handlers, and avoids custom binary socket framing.

questions.question: What is the difference between Optimistic Concurrency Control and Pessimistic Locking?
options: Optimistic concurrency assumes collisions are rare and verifies record version tags upon commit; Pessimistic locking locks records at read time to block other transactions
Optimistic locking requires manual transaction rollback scripts
Pessimistic locking only works in MongoDB
Optimistic locking guarantees 100% higher performance in write-heavy collisions
questions.answer: Optimistic concurrency assumes collisions are rare and verifies record version tags upon commit; Pessimistic locking locks records at read time to block other transactions
questions.explanation: Optimistic control checks a version/timestamp column at write time, aborting if modified. Pessimistic control uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) endpoint in OAuth2 / OpenID Connect?
options: To generate random passwords for new users
To publish public cryptographic keys allowing API resource servers to verify JWT token signatures without calling the identity provider on every request
To export database schemas
To distribute symmetric encryption secrets
questions.answer: To publish public cryptographic keys allowing API resource servers to verify JWT token signatures without calling the identity provider on every request
questions.explanation: JWKS endpoints expose rotating public keys (RSA/EC) that clients and resource servers cache locally to verify asymmetric JWT signatures.

questions.question: In Content Security Policy (CSP), what does the 'strict-dynamic' directive do?
options: It blocks all JavaScript execution entirely
It trusts any script loaded by an already-trusted, nonced script, streamlining modern modular bundler execution while blocking inline injection
It forces HTTPS on all image downloads
It disables iframes on the current domain
questions.answer: It trusts any script loaded by an already-trusted, nonced script, streamlining modern modular bundler execution while blocking inline injection
questions.explanation: strict-dynamic propagates trust from nonced root scripts to dynamically injected child scripts, avoiding brittle domain allowlists.

questions.question: What is the CAP Theorem trade-off in distributed systems?
options: Capacity, Availability, Performance
In the presence of a network partition (P), a distributed data store can guarantee either Consistency (C) or Availability (A), but not both simultaneously
Compute, Application, Persistence
CPU, Architecture, Parallelism
questions.answer: In the presence of a network partition (P), a distributed data store can guarantee either Consistency (C) or Availability (A), but not both simultaneously
questions.explanation: When network splits occur, systems must choose between rejecting requests to preserve single-state consistency (CP) or accepting stale writes to remain available (AP).
